source: BBOC 2025 SEC Betting Preview Part 1+2 (Stuckey/Collin Wilson)

teams.qb_status: Battle — Ty Simpson / Austin Mack / Keylon Russell
teams.key_avoids: Opens at Florida State (wk1 swing); home ULM, Wisconsin; BYE before Georgia (Sept 27); Iron Bowl at Auburn to close. Four SEC opponents (Georgia, Missouri, LSU, Oklahoma) hit Bama off byes.
teams.bboc_notes: Both hosts ~9.4, so no win-total play — but Collin's NATIONAL TITLE pick of the top-10 teams (11-1). Nearly all good news in the offseason: Grubb reunites with DeBoer as OC (Sheridan focuses on QBs), ~8 potential draft picks stayed. Kane Womack's defense was elite in yr1 (2nd in tackling, top-4 finishing drives) and returns loaded at all levels (Deontae Lawson anchor); Collin thinks it's even better. Whole season hinges on the QB battle — Collin believes there's a plan/package for 5-star freshman Keylon Russell held back until needed. Both plan to double down on the title future if Bama loses a game with Simpson starting. WR room loaded (Ryan Williams, Germie Bernard). Watch special teams (lost punter Burnip). Collin: floor 10 wins, ceiling 12 but they'll drop one.

teams.key_avoids: SOS ~44th (soft for Georgia). Only three true SEC road games (at Tennessee early, at Mississippi State, at Auburn off a bye); hosts Alabama + Texas + Ole Miss (both Texas & Bama come in off byes). Neutral vs Georgia Tech + Florida. Hasn't lost at home in five years.
teams.bboc_notes: Both lean UNDER 9.5 (-170): Stuckey projects 9.7, Collin 9.4 — the bet is a 9-win season / no-playoff. #2 recruiting + top-25 portal, but ~96th in returning production. Everything hinges on Gunner Stockton, who never overtook Carson Beck and struggled with pressure; no drop-off to backup (interesting they didn't add a portal QB). OL was 110th, 96th in line yards — couldn't run it; RB Nate Frazier only 2.8 YAC. Improved WR (Zachariah Branch, Noah Thomas) but DL gutted to the NFL, only 67th in havoc (very un-Georgia). Elite special teams (maybe #1) could steal a game. Kirby covers close games; bad as a huge favorite.

teams.qb_status: Returning — Arch Manning (first year as starter)
teams.key_avoids: Opens at Ohio State (the swing game — Stuckey has Texas +3, thinks it closes ~pick/OSU -1). Road at Florida (tricky, off byes for both) + at Georgia; Oklahoma (Red River) + Texas A&M to close. Hosts Arkansas + Vandy (soft). SOS 15th.
teams.bboc_notes: Both project 9.73 — lean under 9.5 (-180) or nothing. ~85th in returning production; lost a ton to the NFL. Arch Manning hyped but unproven — Stuckey warns to pump the brakes on Heisman/greatness talk in year one, though his RPO/legs could fix Sark's red-zone woes. OL down from ~160 starts to 45 (lost Banks/Conner/Williams/Majors) — Goosby a possible 1st-rounder at LT but interior questions. DL takes a step back (lost top-5 DTs; leaning on Purdue transfers) though back-seven fine (Taaffe, Muhammad). Stuckey: 'wipe the win total' — it comes down to the Ohio State opener; beat OSU and 11-1 is live, lose it and ceiling is 10-2. Collin likes Texas +130 to reach the SEC title game.

teams.key_avoids: Starts UTSA, Utah State, at Notre Dame; hosts Auburn, Mississippi State, Florida; road at Arkansas + at LSU (back-to-back travel) + at Texas + at Missouri. Can stack early wins. There is an under-8.5 on DK -150.
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT — Stuckey projects 8.5 and buys the OVER/upside (SEC & playoff longshots, taking Notre Dame out of it); Collin projects just under 8, thinks 8 is the number, sees the schedule capping the ceiling. Top-10 recruiting/portal/returning production. Run game should be ELITE (LaDavian Moss healthy — led FBS in YAC before injury — behind maybe the best OL in the country, Trey Zuhn; 160 starts back). Passing is the question (lost top-4 WRs; Concepcion from NC State + freshmen must pop; Reed 117th on-target). Elko takes over DC play-calling in yr2 to fix a defense that was 109th in tackling. The whole bet is 'Elko fixes the D → lean on the run game.'

teams.key_avoids: One of the ten hardest schedules; road games at Clemson (opener), Ole Miss, Alabama, Oklahoma. Faces only four new-QB opponents. Alabama makes LSU a ~7.5-pt home dog.
teams.bboc_notes: Stuckey buys the UPSIDE (not the win total: he's ~8, Collin 8.8, both pass over-8.5 -140) — bets SEC/playoff futures instead. The one QB in the conference both fully trust is Nussmeier; loaded weapons + backfield (Caden Durham, watch Harlem Berry). Whole season = the rebuilt OL (lost 4 to NFL) getting a run game going, which they utterly lacked in 2024. #1 portal class helps the defense (Collin loves CB Mansoor Delane, Houston S Tanner Halsey, DL Patrick Payton) though they lose all four DL starters. Key: get old-Harold-Perkins back to outside LB (Whit Weeks a boom/bust MLB, 12.9% miss-tackle rate). Collin distrusts DC Blake Baker (career-poor tackling/contested-catch). Collin's Game of the Year: LSU (pick) at Ole Miss — fresh off a cupcake vs Ole Miss's dogfight with Tulane.

teams.key_avoids: One of the five hardest schedules. SEC road: LSU, Texas, Tennessee, Ole Miss; also Notre Dame + at Memphis in non-con; MUST-win Arkansas State in Little Rock. Very few comfortable wins after the first two weeks (maybe Mississippi State at home).
teams.bboc_notes: Effectively a FADE — Collin (Arkansas fan with locker-room sources) projects 4.7 and is under 5.5; Stuckey higher at 5.25 but 'right on market,' still under-leaning. Petrino yr2 could help Taylen Green (showed up +15 lbs muscle; best trait is off-schedule playmaking, RPO reads a problem). Likes Omega Blake (Charlotte WR, 3.3 YPRR) and LT Corey Robinson (PFF top-3 pass-blocking tackle). But the DL generates NO pressure (Collin set the o/u at 9.5 sacks) and the pass D 'will be horrific.' Off-field is combustible: Pittman a lame duck (buyout math), Petrino nearly fist-fought DC Travis Williams in practice, NIL money going to baseball/basketball. 'Could all fall apart quickly.'

teams.key_avoids: One of the ten hardest schedules. SEC road: Auburn, South Carolina, Georgia, Vandy + at Louisville; hosts Tennessee, Florida, Texas, Ole Miss. Toledo + Eastern Michigan two of the first three weeks (Toledo not a gimme). 2-12 in last 14 SEC home games.
teams.bboc_notes: Both PASS for now (both project ~4.86, lean over but waiting on fall-camp intel). Coming off a 4-8 disaster with 63% of the offense brand new, incl. QB Zach Calzada. Collin is the high man: Calzada shaved his pressured turnover-worthy rate from 12.2%→4.5% at Incarnate Word (54:32 BTT:TWP over two years) — a real believer if the OL (experienced transfers incl. G Brown from Arkansas) protects. Weapons thin (Maclin back, adds from Bama/Clemson). Defense transfer-heavy (Wazzu DL David Gusta) but 126th in explosive passing allowed last year — very un-UK. Stoops does his best with no expectations (12-6 ATS off byes); 'vibes are off.' Collin wants positive clean-pocket camp reports on Calzada before buying.

teams.key_avoids: Home games are BRUTAL — Arizona State, Texas, Georgia, Tennessee (all 2024 playoff teams) + Ole Miss. SEC road: Florida, Arkansas, Missouri, Texas A&M. Southern Miss wk1 not a gimme; Alcorn State + NIU the other non-cons. It's all about the first five weeks.
teams.bboc_notes: Both project ~4 wins (Stuckey 4.25, Collin 4.4) and both PASS — over 3.5 is juiced to -155. Reasons for optimism: top-30 in returning production, portal class and recruiting; Shapen back (health), 8 transfer WRs, Fluff Bothwell in the backfield, yr2 of Lebby/schemes. But the trenches cap the jump — only 10 sacks and 38 allowed in 2024. Collin's hard tell: LT Blake Steen was replacement-level and allowed 10 pressures vs Notre Dame/SMU — can't back a team whose blindside tackle yields ~5 pressures/game against SEC edges. Also dead-last in FBS in creating contested catches (a coaching + talent issue). Every SEC game projects as a double-digit dog; the four wins likely come early or not at all.

teams.key_avoids: Could face seven top-20 teams, five away. Opens LIU + USF, then a brutal four-game stretch at LSU, at Miami, Texas, at A&M; then at Georgia (neutral cocktail party) + at Ole Miss. Only six home games (three in the SEC); only two of the SEC bottom-7 (incl. at Kentucky).
teams.key_injury: DJ Lagway — multiple offseason injuries; WRs Wilson/Jackson also banged up in fall
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT — Stuckey projects 7.8 and shows over value but passes on the injury risk; Collin 'can't find eight wins on this schedule' and would play under 7.5 (-ish) but won't fade the ceiling. Everything rides on Lagway's health (18:7 BTT:TWP as a freshman; the offense can cook). OL should be very good (only lost RT; Slaughter a stud C; Damieon George thrived kicked to guard). Freshman WR Dallas Wilson a blue-chip standout; DT Caleb Banks maybe the SEC's best. Defense closed 35th in havoc, 14th in finishing drives despite heavy secondary injuries — lots of experience returns. Both like Lagway (28-1) to win the Heisman if Florida reaches its ceiling / makes the CFP (+350). The relentless injury report is the whole worry.

teams.key_avoids: Schedule broke RIGHT — eight home games; two of four road games are the SEC bottom-2 (at Kentucky early, at Mississippi State late); also gets Arkansas at home. Toughest stretch: at Georgia, at Oklahoma, home South Carolina. Hosts Tulane the week before LSU (terrible spot).
teams.bboc_notes: Stuckey leans UNDER 8.5 (projects ~8.1); not a playoff or 9-win team. The dominant 2024 defense is gutted — lost four DL, LB Chris Paul, three DBs to the NFL (over 50 PBUs gone); 4th-ranked portal class but questionable replacements, nickel takes a step back. OL (their 2024 downfall) loses starters and adds mediocre transfers (Kudus from Arkansas, Diego Pounds back but poor) — run game still a question. Dart gone; Austin Simmons looked good in limited action but is a big unknown. WR Harrison Wallace (Penn St) + De'Zhaun Stribling add help. Collin's Game of the Year is LSU OVER Ole Miss (bad Ole Miss secondary, Tulane hangover). A team the market still prices on brand.

teams.key_avoids: Easy schedule (~50th). Gets the SEC bottom four: home Vandy + Arkansas, at Mississippi State, at Kentucky; also UTSA, UAB, New Mexico State non-con. The four hard games: Georgia, at Alabama, Oklahoma, at Florida.
teams.key_injury: CB Jermod McCoy — lockdown corner, injury; may not be ready for the start
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT — Stuckey UNDER 8.5 (projects 7.85, sees 8-4 max after losing Sampson + a young/thin OL and a DL that lost three to the NFL); Collin higher at 8.9 (likes Aguilar's numbers + returning defense) but PASSES because he prefers the coin-flip opponents (Oklahoma, Florida). A transition/rebuild year: Nico gone, Joey Aguilar (App State, 26:25 BTT:TWP) not a big drop but may throw more picks; most unproven WR room in years; OL has no seniors. Defense is the identity now but took a step back (DL depth, McCoy hurt, safety attrition). Projects as a 2-TD favorite in five of the first six. 'Weird — it's a defensive team now.'

teams.key_avoids: 4th-hardest schedule. SEC road: Ole Miss, LSU, A&M, Missouri; home vs Alabama, Clemson, Oklahoma. Opens vs Virginia Tech (neutral — both hosts bet Va Tech). Two gimmes (SC State, Coastal). Four consecutive brawls LSU/OU/Bama/Ole Miss.
teams.bboc_notes: THE PODCAST BET — both HARD UNDER (Stuckey 6.7, Collin 6.1). 2024's 9-win year was schedule- and luck-fueled (Kentucky/ODU/Akron + banged-up opponents). 14 players off to the NFL rosters — the defense takes a GIANT step back (top-3 DTs, Kennard, two LBs — 212 tackles — all gone) and special teams lost the whole battery (elite punter/long-snapper). OL still a question (lost two best to NFL; Troy/Wake transfers). Sellers electric but 8.7% turnover-worthy rate in a crowded pocket, and lost Rocket Sanders (RBs now tiny). Both taking Virginia Tech in the wk1 opener; will hunt an alt under 7. 'Faves in first five, dogs in next five.'

teams.key_avoids: Opens Baylor, two gimmes, then at Oklahoma — that start defines the season; then at Texas A&M, host Georgia. Back-half breaks: home Missouri, at Arkansas, home Kentucky, at Vandy (the annual Pavia hex — near-automatic loss), Mercer, Iron Bowl at home.
teams.key_injury: K Alex McPherson — health uncertain (worst FG% in FBS last year)
teams.bboc_notes: Both project ~8 but PASS the win total (Vandy is a scheduled loss in their eyes); Collin bets Auburn wk1 ML vs Baylor (Baylor's soft secondary vs Auburn's WRs). Freeze yr3 with 4 straight losing seasons — hot seat, and a 5th would be unacceptable (none since 1950). Top-25 returning production, top-10 portal + recruiting. OL could finally be a strength (~140 starts, all five back). WRs elite (Cam Coleman, Eric Singleton, Malcolm Simmons). Jackson Arnold a good scheme fit but must live up to potential after a brutal OU year (132 pressures). DARK HORSE if they start 3-1/4-0 — 'all the ingredients are there, can they put it together?' Fix the red-zone/turnover/special-teams disasters.

teams.key_avoids: 7th-hardest schedule — plays seven of the SEC top-10 (no Vandy/UK/Miss St/Arkansas) + Michigan in non-con; up to eight ranked opponents. SEC road: Georgia, Texas (Red River neutral); also at Tennessee, at Ole Miss; home Alabama, Auburn, Missouri, LSU. Temple wk3 between Michigan & Auburn.
teams.key_injury: CBs Gentry Williams / DB Robert Spears-Jennings — health monitored; nickel Dolby back from injury
teams.bboc_notes: HOST SPLIT — Collin LOVES OU (projects 8.1, could see Mateer winning the Heisman); Stuckey projects 7.39 (~market), passes, not fully sold on Mateer vs this brutal slate. New OC Ben Arbuckle brings the Wazzu air raid (Venables told to hand off the offense); Mateer forced 54 missed tackles on 149 carries (~Ashton-Jeanty-level), 15 rush TD / only 3 fumbles, safe with the ball. RB Jaydn Ott (Cal) underrated; WRs finally healthy (Deion Burks, Isaiah Sategna from Arkansas). DL + LBs projected the #1 SEC unit despite losing Danny Stutsman, and it's the only thing Venables focuses on. The whole question is nine-plus wins against this schedule; the Auburn game is the swing.

teams.key_avoids: EASIEST SEC schedule. Six home games to start (Central Ark, Kansas, ULL, South Carolina, UMass) + a BYE before hosting Alabama at 5-0; second bye before hosting Texas A&M; home Mississippi State late. SEC road: Auburn, Vandy, Oklahoma, Arkansas.
teams.bboc_notes: Both wanted the UNDER but can't get there — Stuckey 6.9, Collin 7.4 — and PASS (under 7 is juiced -105/-140). Offense 101st in returning production, defense 10th — that's the team. New QB (Beau Pribula from Penn State, 5:1 TD:INT, likely over Horn); lost both tackles to the NFL and all the WRs; RB Ahmad Hardy (ULM) a stud (4.3 YAC, 1000+ yds after contact). Defense should be very good (DC Corey Batoon; ex-Georgia DL; Jalen Catalon adds experience). The scheduling gods love Mizzou — a real chance to start 5-0. Collin: they never lose to Arkansas under Drinkwitz. Zone-read DNA gets stopped only by OU/Bama/A&M/Auburn-caliber fronts.

teams.key_avoids: SEC road: Texas, Tennessee, South Carolina, Alabama (probably 0-fer). Three no-doubt wins (Charleston Southern, Georgia State, Utah State). Home: Missouri (Mizzou on back-to-back travel), LSU (off a bye), Auburn (always beats them), Kentucky. Alabama has this circled for revenge.
teams.key_injury: Diego Pavia — health/durability the biggest concern (took a beating in 2024)
teams.bboc_notes: Stuckey leans OVER 4.5 (-188) small (projects 5.9); Collin exactly 5.0 — the juice sits right where he'd price it. The #1 most-experienced team in the country, top-3 returning production, Pavia back with his old New Mexico State OC calling plays (Jerry Kill consultant). OL loses four starters but Stuckey argues it got BETTER (7 transfers, 4 P4 four-star starters). Run D + LB Langston Patterson solid; the SECONDARY is the real worry (lost both safeties). Pavia is 19-8-1 ATS over two years — 'can't bet against him until the books catch up.' Downside: no one gets surprised by Vandy this year (tape is out; Bama, Sark/Texas out for revenge). Fun to back as a dog, fade as a big favorite.
